data.claim: A periodic re-recall that anchors on the last cadence.ran under recall_recheck:<item> (or the claim), fires only when [cadence].recall_recheck_s has elapsed, and caps itself at recall_recheck_max runs per item, is a complete bounded re-recall -- refuted only if a mid-work heartbeat surfaces nothing new after the interval.
data.falsifier: RC.due(st, item, cfg, at + recall_recheck_s) is False
data.mechanism: The heartbeat (the periodic call an agent already makes during long gates) re-scores the live lessons against the item with services.similar, records cadence.ran, and stops until the interval passes again; matched_lessons filters to [dedupe].show_floor.

chunk_findings.detail: The `except Exception: return ""` path can bypass the cadence bound. If `RC.matched_lessons` raises (e.g. the semantic-scoring/search adapter is unavailable, or a lesson corpus entry is malformed), `_recheck` swallows the error and returns `""` without appending a `cadence.ran` event. The next heartbeat then still sees `recall_recheck:<item>` as due and calls the failing recall path again. For example, with `recall_recheck_s=1800`, two heartbeats one second apart will both invoke `RC.matched_lessons` when the first one raises, and a heartbeat storm will invoke it on every heartbeat, contradicting the documented guarantee that “a heartbeat storm never busy-loops the recall engine.”
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/heartbeat.py:_recheck

chunk_findings.detail: `matched_lessons` builds its candidate set from all live lesson records and then queries that set with the current item’s own text, but it never excludes `item` itself. If the item being heartbeated is a leased lesson (or any record whose `kind` is `lesson`), the lesson is both the query and one of the indexed documents; with no tags, the query text is effectively the same as the record text, so it will match itself and be returned as a “surfaced” lesson. For example, a claimed lesson `L` with empty tags and `show_floor <= 1.0` will have `L` appear in the recheck hits as a lesson the agent has “re-violated,” even though the item is the live task itself, not an external pre-recorded lesson.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/recall.py:matched_lessons

chunk_findings.detail: The second `heartbeat` invocation is not checked for successful exit. The test only asserts that `LESSON_ID` is absent from `out + err`, so a second heartbeat that fails with a non-zero exit code but whose error message does not contain the lesson id still passes. For example, if the new cadence logic raises or returns an error when the max-run bound is reached, and the CLI prints a traceback like `cadence max reached` without the lesson id, the test passes even though `heartbeat` itself has regressed.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_recall_recheck.py:test_a_recheck_does_not_busy_loop_two_heartbeats_in_a_row

chunk_findings.detail: This test claims to prove that “the cadence record bounds it in the log,” but it sets `DDFLOW_CADENCE_RECALL_RECHECK_MAX=1`, so the second heartbeat is suppressed by the max-run cap, not by the cadence interval. A buggy `due`/`_recheck` that ignores the last cadence run and uses the original `lease.acquired_at` as the reference would pass this test: the first heartbeat sees zero cadence records and elapsed time `>= 1s`, surfaces the lesson, and records one cadence; the second heartbeat sees one record and max `1`, so it suppresses. With the same buggy logic and max `2`, two heartbeats in the same interval would both surface because elapsed time since `acquired_at` remains `>= 1s`. The test therefore does not catch the main cadence bug it is meant to guard.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_recall_recheck.py:test_a_recheck_does_not_busy_loop_two_heartbeats_in_a_row

chunk_findings.detail: `RC.matched_lessons(...)` is executed before `log.append("cadence.ran", RC.cadence_id(item), ...)`, and the `except Exception` returns `""` without writing that cadence event. If scoring the lessons corpus fails consistently—for example, one pre-recorded lesson has malformed embeddings and `RC.matched_lessons` raises `ValueError` on every call—then no `cadence.ran recall_recheck:<item>` record is ever written. The next heartbeat’s `RC.due(...)` will still see the recheck as due, so every subsequent heartbeat retries the same failing recall. This is exactly the heartbeat-storm/busy-loop the `recall_recheck_s` knob documents as prevented by recording the run before the next scoring waits. The failed attempt should still record a run attempt before returning, or otherwise mark the due state.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/heartbeat.py:_recheck

chunk_findings.detail: After the second `heartbeat` call (`code, out, err = run_cli(repo, "heartbeat", "T1", agent="beta")`), the test never asserts `code == OK`. If the heartbeat crashes on the second call and the traceback does not contain `LESSON_ID`, the test still passes: `LESSON_ID not in out + err` remains true and the prior first heartbeat still leaves exactly one cadence entry. That lets a bug in the bounded recheck cause the next heartbeat to fail without failing this regression test.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_recall_recheck.py:test_a_recheck_does_not_busy_loop_two_heartbeats_in_a_row

chunk_findings.detail: `similar_records(st)` is called in `matched_lessons`, but `similar_records` is not imported or defined in `ddflow/services/recall.py`. When an agent invokes a heartbeat that triggers a re-check (`_recheck`), `RC.matched_lessons` raises a `NameError` (`name 'similar_records' is not defined`), causing the entire heartbeat function to fail or silently catch the exception, completely breaking the periodic lesson re-check feature.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/recall.py:47

chunk_findings.detail: By setting `DDFLOW_CADENCE_RECALL_RECHECK_MAX=0`, the test now relies entirely on a 1-second wall-clock interval measured across two sequential `run_cli` invocations. If the first heartbeat’s remaining work after recording `cadence.ran`, or the second heartbeat’s startup, takes more than 1s (slow CI, disk sync, clock jump), `RC.due` will legitimately see the recheck as due, the second heartbeat will re-surface `LESSON_ID`, and `assert LESSON_ID not in out + err` fails. The previous `MAX=1` masked this timing jitter; the cadence should be tested with a fake/monkeypatched clock or a much larger interval. This also violates the clock-port aspect of [r-adapters].
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_recall_recheck.py:test_a_recheck_does_not_busy_loop_two_heartbeats_in_the_interval

chunk_findings.detail: The revised cadence path still calls `time.time()` directly in `RC.due(...)` rather than going through ddflow’s clock adapter, which [r-adapters] requires for clocks. This keeps the new interval test tied to real wall-clock time: the test must `time.sleep(1.3)` and then run a second heartbeat before the 1-second `recall_recheck_s` window expires. On a loaded CI runner where the second `run_cli` invocation starts more than 1s after the first `cadence.ran`, `RC.due` will correctly return True and re-surface the lesson, making the test fail even though the production logic is correct.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/heartbeat.py:_recheck

chunk_findings.detail: The test is still nondeterministic because the “inside the interval” assertion depends on real subprocess latency and wall-clock time. It sets the recheck interval to 5 seconds, sleeps 5.3 seconds, runs the first heartbeat, then immediately runs the second and asserts `LESSON_ID not in out + err`. If the first heartbeat’s post-`cadence.ran` work (semantic scoring, output, event-log flush) or the second `run_cli` startup takes 5 seconds or more on a loaded CI runner, the second heartbeat will legitimately see the 5-second interval as elapsed, re-run the recheck, re-surface `LESSON_ID`, and the assertion fails. chunk_findings.detail: The `except Exception: return ""` path can bypass the cadence bound. If `RC.matched_lessons` raises (e.g. the semantic-scoring/search adapter is unavailable, or a lesson corpus entry is malformed), `_recheck` swallows the error and returns `""` without appending a `cadence.ran` event. The next heartbeat then still sees `recall_recheck:<item>` as due and calls the failing recall path again. For example, with `recall_recheck_s=1800`, two heartbeats one second apart will both invoke `RC.matched_lessons` when the first one raises, and a heartbeat storm will invoke it on every heartbeat, contradicting the documented guarantee that “a heartbeat storm never busy-loops the recall engine.”
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/heartbeat.py:_recheck

chunk_findings.detail: `matched_lessons` builds its candidate set from all live lesson records and then queries that set with the current item’s own text, but it never excludes `item` itself. If the item being heartbeated is a leased lesson (or any record whose `kind` is `lesson`), the lesson is both the query and one of the indexed documents; with no tags, the query text is effectively the same as the record text, so it will match itself and be returned as a “surfaced” lesson. For example, a claimed lesson `L` with empty tags and `show_floor <= 1.0` will have `L` appear in the recheck hits as a lesson the agent has “re-violated,” even though the item is the live task itself, not an external pre-recorded lesson.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/recall.py:matched_lessons

chunk_findings.detail: The second `heartbeat` invocation is not checked for successful exit. The test only asserts that `LESSON_ID` is absent from `out + err`, so a second heartbeat that fails with a non-zero exit code but whose error message does not contain the lesson id still passes. For example, if the new cadence logic raises or returns an error when the max-run bound is reached, and the CLI prints a traceback like `cadence max reached` without the lesson id, the test passes even though `heartbeat` itself has regressed.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_recall_recheck.py:test_a_recheck_does_not_busy_loop_two_heartbeats_in_a_row

chunk_findings.detail: This test claims to prove that “the cadence record bounds it in the log,” but it sets `DDFLOW_CADENCE_RECALL_RECHECK_MAX=1`, so the second heartbeat is suppressed by the max-run cap, not by the cadence interval. A buggy `due`/`_recheck` that ignores the last cadence run and uses the original `lease.acquired_at` as the reference would pass this test: the first heartbeat sees zero cadence records and elapsed time `>= 1s`, surfaces the lesson, and records one cadence; the second heartbeat sees one record and max `1`, so it suppresses. With the same buggy logic and max `2`, two heartbeats in the same interval would both surface because elapsed time since `acquired_at` remains `>= 1s`. The test therefore does not catch the main cadence bug it is meant to guard.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_recall_recheck.py:test_a_recheck_does_not_busy_loop_two_heartbeats_in_a_row

chunk_findings.detail: `RC.matched_lessons(...)` is executed before `log.append("cadence.ran", RC.cadence_id(item), ...)`, and the `except Exception` returns `""` without writing that cadence event. If scoring the lessons corpus fails consistently—for example, one pre-recorded lesson has malformed embeddings and `RC.matched_lessons` raises `ValueError` on every call—then no `cadence.ran recall_recheck:<item>` record is ever written. The next heartbeat’s `RC.due(...)` will still see the recheck as due, so every subsequent heartbeat retries the same failing recall. This is exactly the heartbeat-storm/busy-loop the `recall_recheck_s` knob documents as prevented by recording the run before the next scoring waits. The failed attempt should still record a run attempt before returning, or otherwise mark the due state.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/heartbeat.py:_recheck

chunk_findings.detail: After the second `heartbeat` call (`code, out, err = run_cli(repo, "heartbeat", "T1", agent="beta")`), the test never asserts `code == OK`. If the heartbeat crashes on the second call and the traceback does not contain `LESSON_ID`, the test still passes: `LESSON_ID not in out + err` remains true and the prior first heartbeat still leaves exactly one cadence entry. That lets a bug in the bounded recheck cause the next heartbeat to fail without failing this regression test.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_recall_recheck.py:test_a_recheck_does_not_busy_loop_two_heartbeats_in_a_row

chunk_findings.detail: `similar_records(st)` is called in `matched_lessons`, but `similar_records` is not imported or defined in `ddflow/services/recall.py`. When an agent invokes a heartbeat that triggers a re-check (`_recheck`), `RC.matched_lessons` raises a `NameError` (`name 'similar_records' is not defined`), causing the entire heartbeat function to fail or silently catch the exception, completely breaking the periodic lesson re-check feature.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/recall.py:47

chunk_findings.detail: By setting `DDFLOW_CADENCE_RECALL_RECHECK_MAX=0`, the test now relies entirely on a 1-second wall-clock interval measured across two sequential `run_cli` invocations. If the first heartbeat’s remaining work after recording `cadence.ran`, or the second heartbeat’s startup, takes more than 1s (slow CI, disk sync, clock jump), `RC.due` will legitimately see the recheck as due, the second heartbeat will re-surface `LESSON_ID`, and `assert LESSON_ID not in out + err` fails. The previous `MAX=1` masked this timing jitter; the cadence should be tested with a fake/monkeypatched clock or a much larger interval. This also violates the clock-port aspect of [r-adapters].
